global: RESEARCH FIRST (accuracy and curiosity gate; before any line is re-narrated): verify and add two claims to research/claims.json with sources fetched and read. (1) mk1-trained: the Mark I was trained by being shown examples and corrected on its errors, not programmed with the rule for each shape (Rosenblatt 1958, Psychological Review 65(6); Wikipedia 'Perceptron'; NMAH object 334414). This gates the L0105 rewrite. (2) mk1-patchboard: the photocells were connected to the association units through a patch board with randomly wired connections. This backs L0103 and L0105b. Then cite the claims per shot in script.json.

STORY AND RE-LOCK ORDER: apply the line rewrites (L0103, L0104, L0105 if verified, L0105b, L0106, L0108), then re-narrate only those lines, re-lock the clock, re-fit m01 and re-anchor s02 and s03. Add two per-line fields to script.json and honour them in film-narrate and the mix: preGap (default 0.45 s; L0104 0.8 s, L0108 about 2.6 s) and levelDb (L0101 -3 dB, L0108 -1.5 dB), applied after the word rides and before the speech compressor. Check that L0101 peaks at or below about -14 LUFS momentary in the master and that the D-major bloom stays the loudest non-speech moment. Runtime ceiling 66 s ('about a minute'); if it runs over, shorten the bookend hold before cutting any new line.

MIX DUCK: the mixer measures 5.52 dB of ducking against m01's 3 dB target, and QA passes it. Treat a cue's depthDb as a ceiling (lower the ratio or raise the threshold until the measured depth is within 1 dB of the target), and make QA warn when the measured duck exceeds the target by more than 1.5 dB.

issuesMerged.problem: "Each lit cell tugs the needle through its dial" says each photocell has its own dial wired straight to the needle. The film's own bible says the Mark I reached the response unit 'through a randomly wired association layer', and the weights (claim mk1-weights) sat on those connections, not on the 400 cells. The picture is already more faithful than the line: at 34.29 s the lit cells' threads pass through the patch tangle and fan out to several dials (about 80 on the board, not 400). The 'an illustration of the rule' caption covers the simplified board, but this narrated sentence is about 'it', the Mark I.

"Behind it ran a nest of wires" is supported only by the bible ('patch board of tangled cables'), not by research/claims.json, which the brief makes the only allowed source. Racks, dials and motors are covered by mk1-weights; the wiring is not.

The picture during 'It could learn only simple patterns' (48.97-51.6 s) contradicts the line. The 'both learned shapes ghosted side by side' plate draws the short horizontal bar and the vertical bar almost touching, so it reads as one new L/T-shaped figure. Meanwhile the needle still sits on HORIZONTAL, the lantern is still lit and the caption still says 'try 5 · said horizontal · right' (verified at 50.3 and 50.8 s). A 15-year-old sees the machine succeed on a harder-looking shape at the exact moment the narrator says it could only learn simple ones. Then the iris closes on the lantern, and the limit is never shown.

Depth stops at 'it could learn only simple patterns'. The film never says who showed the limit or what it cost, even though claims.json now carries limit-linear (Minsky and Papert's 1969 'Perceptrons'; the decline of neural-network research in the 1970s). Belief, dissent and its duration are the lens's history test, and the evidence is already verified. The jump from 1960 to 'today's neural networks' leaves no sense that the idea nearly died, which is also why curiosity stays at 6.5.

'And the total decides' (33.12-34.39 s) needs a threshold, but the gauge's decision line is an unlabelled top-centre tick. A young viewer cannot see why the needle's position means VERTICAL, and an expert notices the threshold is missing from the picture of the mk1-sum rule.

The 'right answer' that every nudge moves toward is never shown before the verdict. The retina shows a bar, and the viewer only learns which answer was correct from the 'wrong' caption after the fact. The supervision signal, the teacher's answer, is the heart of error-correction, and right now it is implied.
'Its descendants, today's neural networks' (52.38-55.4 s) plays over the 1960 lab bookend. Nothing on screen says 'descendants' or 'today', so the lineage claim is heard but not seen.

As written, 'the dials that had a say a little toward the right answer' parses as 'had a say a little'. The spoken take pauses after 'say' (38.76 to 39.71 s), but the caption (VTT cue 8) runs 'that had a say a little / toward the right answer' with no comma, which trips readers watching with captions on.

The mix reports a duck depth of 5.52 dB against a 3 dB target (mix/loudness.json). The QA check passes it, but the quiet celesta 'wrong' cells (E6/F6 at 42.91-43.07 s) that teach the error beat may sink further than the composer planned.
Lens note: AlexNet and the transformer cannot be explained in a one-minute Mark I short, and they are not scored against this film.

The proof of discrimination is muddied by the 'simple patterns' pair. At about 50.0-50.8 s, while the caption still reads 'try 5 · said horizontal · right' and the needle points at HORIZONTAL, the retina morphs into a single '-|' glyph: the horizontal bar shifted left and a vertical bar beside it on the same 20x20 plate. A viewer reads it as the machine now seeing a strange new shape and calling it horizontal. It is not read as 'the two shapes it learned', so the clean before/after that try 5 just set up gets blurred right before the iris.

The second triumph has no room. Try 5's flare (about 49.3-49.7 s) lands under 'It could learn only simple patterns' (which starts at 48.97). The film's proof that it really learned is spoken over by the deflating limit, and the D-major bloom is already closing by 49.0. The emotional sequence 'right, and right again... and yet only simple patterns' is compressed into one overlapping moment, so neither the joy nor the honest limit fully lands.

Curiosity is still the weakest lens. The film never plants the question that makes the perceptron astonishing: nobody told it which shape was which, and it found the rule from its own mistakes. It goes straight from a 20-second parts inventory (s02: eye, wires, dials, name) to 'Show it a shape, and it guesses'. The viewer is never made to wonder 'how could a machine possibly learn that?' before the answer arrives, so the payoff feels like a demonstration rather than a revelation.

The second correct answer (the try-5 lantern flare) has no musical answer. The bloom on 'right' closes by 49.0, and the spectrogram shows the bed simply resuming. Musically the film says 'right' once, which undersells the proof that it learned both shapes.

The bookend's human beat is inert. From 53.5 to 59.8 s Rosenblatt holds the same outstretched presenting pose he struck in s02 while 'Its descendants, today's neural networks, still learn from mistakes' plays. The last emotional image belongs to a statue, not to a person who has just watched his machine learn.

The verdict captions that carry the struggle and the comparison are still small italic type. The ghosted 'try 1 · said vertical · wrong' under try 5 is roughly 15-18 px high at 1080p and faint, and it is the one piece of text that turns try 5 into a before/after.

Carried over from round 1, still partly open. From about 2.5 s the eye, its stand and all three racks are shown in clear silhouette under the title, so s02's part-by-part reveal ('Its eye... Behind it... racks of dials') repeats what has already been seen and slows the setup.

New retina glitch in the tail, under the closing line L0108 ('It could learn only simple patterns'). From about 50.0 to 51.3 s the try-5 horizontal bar shrinks from the right while a vertical column grows at about col 16, so the grid shows an L/T hybrid and then a short dash plus a vertical bar. Meanwhile the caption still reads 'try 5 · said horizontal · right' and the needle sits on HORIZONTAL. It looks like a sixth presentation (or the ghost of an earlier shape) starting during the curtain and push-out. It reintroduces the round-1 overlap problem and contradicts the caption at the moment the film states its limit.

The Rosenblatt acting still misses the name beat. He is absent at 18.0 s and mid-stride at 19.0 s, so he still comes in from the right frame edge. His one presenting gesture lands at 21.0 to 22.0 s on 'built', with the arm thrown back toward the racks while his face points right, toward the window. On 'Frank Rosenblatt's' (22.85 to 24.2 s) and through the name card he faces away from the machine. His arms hang stiff with splayed fingers, the rear arm is hyperextended, and the legs read as one fused column. He has no tie, cuffs or pencil, and a thin full-body outline is still visible. Next to the reference figures (period silhouettes with costume detail, poised and turned toward each other or an object) the puppet reads as a generic mannequin.

The lab set (sets/lab.ts, used by s01, s02 and the s03 bookend) is better than in round 1, with cable garlands, louvres, haze and a stool and chair. But it is still below the reference. Every rack, window and stand carries the same thin light outline. The dial racks are identical repeated grids. The foreground stool and chair (21.0 s) are the same value as the racks, so the planes do not separate. The reference gets its depth from near-black foreground furniture, ornamented mid-plane cut-outs and a hazed back wall.

Some verdict captions arrive after their words. At 43.6 s the 'try 3 · said vertical · wrong' caption is barely visible while 'wrong again' is spoken (43.54 s), and it reaches full strength only around 44.2 s. At 47.0 s the 'try 4 · said vertical · right' caption is faint just before 'right' (47.06 s) and reaches full strength around 47.6 s. Try 1 (35.6 s) and try 2 (42.6 s) land on time.

The before/after comparison barely reads. The ghost line 'try 1 · said vertical · wrong' under the try-5 caption (49.6 s) is small (about 22 px), grey on amber, and close to illegible at 1080p. The retina gives no visual echo of try 1, so 'same shape, now right' rests on a line of faint text.

The bookend (53.4 to 59.2 s) is a well-composed frame: Rosenblatt facing the eye, the stimulus card and the eye both showing the bar, and the title back. But it is nearly static for about 5 s under 'Its descendants, today's neural networks, still learn from mistakes', so no visual beat lands on 'descendants' (52.77 s), 'neural networks' (54.57 s) or 'mistakes' (56.99 s). The title simply sits there.

The s01-to-s02 crossfade (5.8 to 6.3 s) dissolves between two near-identical framings of the eye on its stand, with the same windows and a slightly tighter scale. It reads as a soft jump-cut rather than a change of view. The eye is also already lit with its bar from about 3.5 s, which spends the 'Its eye' reveal (6.92 s) early.

The protagonist is introduced with a sentence that sounds like a misreading when heard: 'It was the Mark I Perceptron, built by psychologist Frank Rosenblatt's project.' The ear parses 'built by psychologist Frank Rosenblatt', then hits the possessive and '...'s project' (24.17-24.80) as an afterthought. That fragment also lands where the M4 cello was meant to answer the name: the cue notes say the cello A2 at 24.79 now 'answers project' rather than the name. The line copies claim mk1-builder word for word, which reads fine on paper but not aloud.

The name is still not verified for the new voice (Peter, speed 0.8). QA stt is 'skip', and voice/lexicon.json says ROH-zen-blat is 'still to be confirmed by ear'. The timing (0.81 s) and level (-23.9 dB, the same as 'psychologist') look healthy, but this is the only proper name in the film and nothing has checked it.

The per-line normaliser removed the intended delivery dynamics. Every line sits between -18.4 and -19.7 dB RMS in the master. L0101 ('quiet, a storyteller beginning') is the single loudest momentary point of the film (-11.3 LUFS M at 2.1 s), louder than the D-major bloom (-13.2 at 48.0). It enters from near-silence (music -36 LUFS M at 1.1 s), so the first word lands hard on a black screen. L0108 ('quieter, reflective') is no quieter than the explanatory lines. Round 1's fix asked for explicit per-line offsets for intended dynamics, and none were added.

m01 asks for depthDb 3, but the mixer measures 5.52 dB of ducking under 46.1 s of speech, and QA passes it anyway. The cue was pre-levelled for a 3 dB duck. The low under-speech machine figures (the pizz 'sum' D2-A2-D3-E3 under 'tugs the needle', the three A2 'nudge' plucks at 36.93) end up about 15 dB under the voice (music -26.5 raw, about -32 in the master vs about -17.5 speech on 'nudge'). These are the score's sonic stand-in for the motors, and at that level they are probably lost.

A hesitation inside an idiom: 'the dials that had a [0.28 s] say [0.45 s] a little toward the right answer' (pauses at 38.76 and 39.71). The first pause splits 'had a | say', so the clause sounds unsure. The sentence is already the longest in the film (6.6 s) and hard to parse by ear ('a say a little').

The soundtrack is still voice plus score only. The picture shows motors turning dials, needles swinging and a lantern flaring on 'right', yet there is no relay click, motor whirr or tube hum anywhere. With the duck overshoot, the pizz stand-ins are also buried under speech.

Inside each narration chunk the lines are still joined by the same mechanical 0.45 s gap (L0102 > L0103 > L0104, L0105 > L0105b > L0106). The turn from describing the machine to naming it (17.57 to 18.02) gets no more air than a mid-description breath, so 'It was the Mark I Perceptron' runs straight on from 'motors could turn'.

summary: FAIL (round 2). Mean 7.43 (round 1: 6.65), with sync now at the bar (8.0) and accuracy just over (8.08). Depth (6.42) and curiosity (6.75) are still lowest, followed by story (7.25). No critical issues. Most round-1 fixes landed. The high-leverage fixes: (1) remove the tail retina morph at about 50 s (confirmed on the render) and give try 5 its own clear air before L0108; (2) deepen L0108 with the verified Minsky and Papert 1969 limit (no causal verb) and plant the curiosity question in L0105 ('Nobody gave it the rule'), gated on a new mk1-trained claim; (3) re-word L0104 so the name ends the sentence, and STT-check 'Rosenblatt'; (4) re-block Rosenblatt in s02 so he faces the machine on his name; (5) fix the mix duck overshoot and add per-line preGap and levelDb. Runtime ceiling 66 s.
